summary: Baccalieu Island North Point Light: a brick tower shown in 1858 with Stevenson apparatus, kept by four generations of Ryans, now a steel tower in an ecological reserve.

lens.type: catadioptric holophote (revolving apparatus, nine lamps; 1858 Stevenson apparatus)
lens.note: Lighthouse Friends calls it the first use of a catadioptric holophote; the claim is not confirmed by other sources in hand

structures.note: Stands 25 ft (7.6 m); focal plane 443 ft (135 m) for the 1858 light. Lighthouse Friends gives the tower's status only by implication (demolition was planned and protested); a current source is needed to confirm it still stands.

structures.type: square skeleton tower, red and white rectangular daymark
structures.note: Coast Guard list: 19.2 m. Lighthouse Friends says the 1990s tower is 45 ft (about 13.7 m). The record gives 1990 built.
Square two-storey dwelling joined to the tower by a covered way; painted white with a red roof; enlarged by a two-storey addition in 1882
Second dwelling built at the north station

staffing.note: Keepers moved to the southwest station after the 1965 fire; the north light automated (Lighthouse Friends)

access.note: Part of Baccalieu Island Ecological Reserve. Grounds open, tower closed (Lighthouse Friends). Boat landings at Ned Walsh's Cove and London Cove; seabird nesting areas closed to visitors April 1 to October 30 except scientific researchers and permit holders; aircraft may not land in the reserve or fly below 300 m in that season.

visit.note: Visible from shore across Baccalieu Tickle from Red Head Cove. Bay de Verde Heritage House exhibit (opened 1999) has displays on the island and lighthouse.

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (owner); island within Baccalieu Island Ecological Reserve

corrections.proposed: Tower closed; grounds open (Lighthouse Friends). Island is part of Baccalieu Island Ecological Reserve: boat landings at Ned Walsh's Cove and London Cove; seabird nesting areas closed to visitors April 1 to October 30
corrections.why: 'Closed' does not describe the grounds or the reserve's rules. The tower is closed; the grounds and most of the island are open at other times.

corrections.proposed: Canadian Coast Guard (owner and operator); the island lies within Baccalieu Island Ecological Reserve
corrections.why: Lighthouse Friends: the lighthouse is owned by the Canadian Coast Guard. The reserve is the land designation, not the operator.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record says sources differ on whether the light is still lit. The Coast Guard list gives the North Point light as year round, flashing every six seconds. Lighthouse Friends describes it as flashing every six seconds today. The light is lit.
The record's 176 m is the Coast Guard's figure for the present tower. The 443 ft (135 m) in Lighthouse Friends is the focal plane of the 1858 light.

notes_for_editor: (1) Almost all history (1857 to 1990) comes from one secondary source, Lighthouse Friends, which cites the Journal of the House of Assembly and the Encyclopedia of Newfoundland and Labrador without quoting them. The Newfoundland records before 1949 are not in the corpus, and the National Library of Scotland Stevenson papers catalogue (manuscripts.nls.uk/subjects/5064) returns 403, so the Stevenson and Baccalieu links are not independently confirmed. (2) Lighthouse Friends' keeper list has no dates for five names, and no dates for the 1950s to 1960s keepers beyond Felix Noonan (at least 1963). Named later keepers are included only as the source prints them. (3) The record's 1990 tower (19.2 m, CCG) and the Lighthouse Friends '45-foot' tower (about 13.7 m) disagree. The story gives both. (4) The story's 'stands near the original tower' follows Lighthouse Friends' present-tense 'located near the original lighthouse'. No source states outright that the 1858 tower still stands; the 1858 structure's status 'standing' rests on that implication (and on the demolition passage) and needs a current source before publishing. (5) The Bay de Verde exhibit's claim of 'more than 20 documented wrecks' and 200 lives lost is not sourced to named wrecks; it is attributed as the exhibit's and no individual wreck is used. (6) The Bay de Verde exhibit gives the south-end light and fog horn as 1904, Lighthouse Friends gives a diaphone fog alarm in August 1906 at the southwest station. The story does not use either date. (7) The Southwest Point light is a separate station; its keepers and 2002 de-staffing are left to that record. (8) The US Life-Saving Service tables list 'Baccalieu Island' among places where American vessels stranded (1890s). The counts cannot be read by column in the OCR, so they are not used. (9) The ICH blog and Wikipedia were not used as sources. (10) Newspapers were not searched: the Newfoundland press is not in Chronicling America. (11) Tower type: the record says 'conical_masonry, brick'; Lighthouse Friends says 'circular red brick'. The story uses 'circular'. Not in the corrections list (shape, not a listed error type), so flagged here for a human to decide. (12) Photos: none proposed.
